title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Trend, Volume & Momentum Opportunity

epigraph.quote: When a former Stage 2 leader slips beneath both its 50-day moving average and its 10-week EMA, the tape is no longer giving you a free ride — it is telling you to step back and let structural support prove itself.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Tape Discipline

web_blocks.html: NSE:MARINE's tape has weakened since November 13. The stock has shifted from Stage 2 into Stan Weinstein Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) [24]. On the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close, MARINE ended at ₹406.95 (+0.48% 1D, -3.79% 1W, -17.09% off its ₹490.85 high). It already sat below its 50-day SMA (₹422.77) and 10-week EMA (₹410.60), with 7 distribution days over 25 sessions. By the live 2026-11-25 TradingView snapshot, price fell to ₹400.60 (-1.56% 1D, -18.39% off the high). That confirms a WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT_RETEST posture [24].

web_blocks.takeaway: MARINE has transitioned from Stage 2 into Stage 3 (WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT_RETEST), trading -0.94% below its 10W EMA (₹404.40) and -5.12% below its 50D SMA (₹422.22) with no 4H turn confirmed (4H RSI 42.58). Structural support sits at ₹353.54–₹364.30, and our upward-only invalidation stop ratchets from ₹313.40 to ₹327.13.

web_blocks.html: Market breadth and flow signals also favor patience. On the 2026-11-23 NSE session, Indian equities stayed in an Uptrend (narrow breadth) on Nifty 50. Roughly 55.2% of the 500-stock pool traded above their 50-DMA, and 48.2% above their 200-DMA, with 3 distribution days and 7 of 11 sectors healthy. Inside MARINE, FIIs rose to 2.08% and DIIs to 1.08% by September 2026 [5]. However, promoter entity KDU Enterprises sold 42 lakh shares (3.01% of equity) into the rally [5]. Even after November 16's ₹233.21 Cr order win, price failed to reclaim its 50-day SMA (₹422.22), confirming overhead supply [28].

MARINE is NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID because it is outside the NSE F&O segment. Traders cannot buy call spreads or hedge with puts; all exposure is cash equity. On the 4-hour chart (DISLOCATION_AT_MAJOR_SHELF), price at ₹400.60 sits below the 4H 20-EMA (₹411.78) and 4H 50-SMA (₹414.44). 4H RSI is 42.58 versus Daily RSI of 45.18, so no intraday turn is confirmed. If ₹395–₹400 breaks, the next major shelf is Pivot S1 (₹358.92; zone ₹353.54–₹364.30) above the rising 30-week SMA (₹339.24) [24].

Our upward-only stop-loss ratchet protects the Zerodha holding without panic selling. Since November 13, the 30-week SMA climbed from ₹327.52 to ₹339.24, and the 200-day SMA rose from ₹286.50 to ₹294.65. That lifts our structural stop from ₹313.40 to ₹327.13 (+4.38% ratchet). Across naval and power peers on November 25, MAZDOCK, COCHINSHIP, GRSE, CGPOWER, VOLTAMP, and TARIL are all in Stage 4. Only BEL holds Stage 2. MARINE's Stage 3 base above its rising 30W SMA supports HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP at ₹327.13 on our 1.19% stake while blocking new capital.

book_paragraphs: Turn now from the valuation spreadsheet to the live price chart, because something important changed between our November 13 baseline and today's refresh. Two weeks ago, Marine Electricals sat cleanly in a Stage 2 uptrend, resting right on its 50-day moving average. Today, the tape has shifted gears into Stan Weinstein Stage 3 — a topping and consolidation phase where overhead supply is actively absorbing good news.

Look at the two verified session marks. On the official November 23, 2026 NSE ledger close, MARINE finished at ₹406.95, already below its 50-day SMA (₹422.77) and 10-week EMA (₹410.60) with seven distribution days logged over the prior twenty-five sessions. By the live November 25, 2026 TradingView snapshot, price drifted further to ₹400.60 — down 18.39% from its ₹490.85 fifty-two-week high, sitting 0.94% below its 10-week EMA (₹404.40) and 5.12% below its 50-day SMA (₹422.22).

Think about what it tells you when a company announces ₹233.21 Cr in fresh hyperscale data-center and shipyard orders on November 16, files an upbeat investor presentation on November 23, and the stock STILL cannot reclaim its 50-day moving average. That is textbook Stage 3 digestion: early buyers and momentum funds are using order headlines to distribute shares, while fresh institutional buyers refuse to chase 70x trailing earnings.

On the multi-timeframe dashboard, the message is unambiguous: WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT_RETEST. Daily RSI has cooled to 45.18, 4-hour RSI sits at 42.58 with price stuck beneath both the 4-hour 20-EMA (₹411.78) and 4-hour 50-SMA (₹414.44), and there is no confirmed intraday turn. Meanwhile, because MARINE is not in the NSE F&O segment, there is no liquid options chain to express a defined-risk bounce trade — every rupee of risk is pure cash equity.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: WHEN GOOD NEWS CANNOT LIFT THE CHART
book_callouts.text: One of the most reliable signals in market history is how a stock reacts to great news. When MARINE wins ₹233.21 Cr in STT Global Data Centres and Ganges Shipyard orders and still trades below its 50-day SMA and 10-week EMA, the tape is confirming what our valuation chapter already proved: the good news was priced in at ₹490.

book_subsections.title: Multi-Timeframe Anatomy: Weekly Trend Intact, Daily & 4H Dislocated
paragraphs: Dissecting NSE:MARINE across three timeframes on November 25, 2026 keeps us from making emotional errors. On the Weekly chart, the primary bull trend has not yet broken: price at ₹400.60 still sits +18.09% above the rising 30-week SMA (₹339.24) and +35.96% above the 200-day SMA (₹294.65), with Weekly RSI at a healthy 58.46. Volume on the latest pullback (6.48 lakh shares vs 11.85 lakh 30-day average, a 0.55x ratio) is moderate rather than panic-driven capitulation.

On the Daily and 4-Hour charts, however, momentum has rolled over into Stage 3. Price is trapped beneath the 20-day SMA (₹415.07), the 50-day SMA (₹422.22), and the 10-week EMA (₹404.40). On the 4-hour chart, the stock sits in a Dislocation-at-Major-Shelf posture with no confirmed turn (4H RSI 42.58, close below 4H EMA20 ₹411.78). Until buyers defend the structural support shelf at ₹353.54–₹364.30 (centered on Pivot S1 ₹358.92) or reclaim ₹422+ on expanding volume, chasing here is fighting the tape.

book_subsections.title: The Upward-Only Stop-Loss Ratchet & Position Sizing Math
paragraphs: A major operational change occurred in our actual Zerodha portfolio since November 13: the holding expanded from 25 tracking shares to 125 shares, carrying a cost basis of ₹51,604.15 (₹412.83 average cost). At the November 23 NSE ledger close of ₹406.95, the position is worth ₹50,868.75 (-₹735.40 / -1.43%, 1.19% of the ₹42.64 lakh IN portfolio); at the live November 25 TradingView close of ₹400.60, it marks at ₹50,075.00 (-₹1,529.15 / -2.96%).

Because this is still a modest 1.19% portfolio weight and the primary 30-week SMA (₹339.24) is still rising, we apply our mechanical upward-only stop-loss ratchet. As the 30-week SMA climbed from ₹327.52 to ₹339.24, the live TradingView structural invalidation stop moved up from ₹313.40 to ₹327.13 (+4.38% ratchet). At ₹327.13, maximum downside from the ₹400.60 live close across 125 shares is ₹9,183.75 — just 0.22% of total portfolio net worth. That gives the position enough room to breathe through its ₹24.21 (6.04%) 14-day ATR while drawing an unbreakable line against a Stage 4 collapse.

book_subsections.title: Sector Breadth & Relative Strength Against Peer Shipbuilders
paragraphs: Zooming out to the November 23, 2026 Indian market regime adds vital context. The Nifty 50 remains in an Uptrend (narrow breadth), with 55.2% of the 500-stock universe above their 50-DMA, 48.2% above their 200-DMA, and 7 of 11 sectors above key moving averages. Yet inside MARINE's specific peer cluster on November 25, tape damage is widespread: Mazagon Dock, Cochin Shipyard, GRSE, CG Power, Voltamp Transformers, and TARIL are all mired in Stage 4 downtrends.

Only Bharat Electronics (BEL) holds a clean Stage 2 uptrend (BUY_AT_CMP_NO_FOMO at ₹404.30). MARINE's Stage 3 holding pattern is therefore a middle-of-the-pack survivor — too resilient above its rising 30-week SMA to panic-dump at a 1.19% weight, yet far too bruised below its 50-day SMA and 10-week EMA to attract a single rupee of fresh capital.
